paras.en: [[7:17|Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit|Sic omnis arbor bona, fructus bonos facit]], provided it is ordered to bearing fruit and not rather to other uses. Or by fruit is understood every advantage that comes from the tree. [[7:17|and the evil tree bringeth forth evil fruit|Mala autem arbor fructus malos facit]]. These things are asserted principally of men, understanding by the good tree a right will, or a just man; by the evil tree a perverse will, or a vicious man. The good man, then, as such, bears good fruits; and the evil man, evil ones. [[7:18|A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit|Non potest arbor bona fructus malos facere]], in so far as it is good; so neither can a virtuous man, as such, do evil works. Yet he can become evil and sin. [[7:18|neither can an evil tree bring forth good fruit|Neque arbor mala, ut talis, fructus bonos facere]], as such. So the wicked man, as such, cannot do good works, although he can become good. The Saviour, then, speaks of the good and evil tree formally, not materially. Hence propositions of this kind are true in the composed sense, and not in the divided sense [that is, a good tree, while it remains good, cannot bear evil fruit; not that a tree which is now good can never bear evil fruit].

paras.t: Omnis arbor, hoc est quilibet homo adultus, rationisque compos, quæ non facit fructum bonum, observando præcepta, excidetur a consortio electorum : juxta illud, Tollatur impius, ne videat gloriam Dei; et in ignem infernalem mittetur, in judicio particulari, quantum ad animam, in judicio vero universali, cum anima et corpore. Si ergo peccatum omissionis meretur ignem inferni, peccatum commissionis quam horribiliter punietur ? Unde dicit Salvator : Omnem palmitem in me non ferentem fructum, tollet eum, et in ignem mittet. Ex his infertur intenta conclusio : Igitur ex fructibus eorum cognoscetis eos.
paras.en: [[7:19|Every tree|Omnis arbor]], that is, every adult man having the use of reason, [[7:19|that bringeth not forth good fruit|quæ non facit fructum bonum]] by keeping the precepts, [[7:19|shall be cut down|excidetur]] from the fellowship of the elect, according to the words, Let the wicked be taken away, lest he see the glory of God [cf. Is 26:10]; [[7:19|and shall be cast into the fire|et in ignem infernalem mittetur]] of hell, at the particular judgment as to the soul, and at the universal judgment with soul and body. If, then, the sin of omission deserves the fire of hell, how horribly will the sin of commission be punished? Hence the Saviour says: [[John 15:2|Every branch in me, that beareth not fruit, he will take away|Omnem palmitem in me non ferentem fructum, tollet eum]], and cast into the fire [cf. John 15:6]. From these things the intended conclusion is drawn: [[7:20|Wherefore by their fruits you shall know them|Igitur ex fructibus eorum cognoscetis eos]].

paras.t: Quod autem sine fructibus bonis nemo queat salvari, pandit Salvator subjungens: Non omnis qui dicit mihi ex fide informi : Domine, Domine, sicut fatuæ virgines; intrabit in regnum. cœlorum : quia non sufficit nuda confessio oris. Sed videtur contrarium illud Apostoli : Nemo potest dicere, Dominus Jesus, nisi in Spiritu Sancto ; et rursus, Corde creditur ad justitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem. Dicendum, quod Apostolus sumit Dicere, proprie, pro enuntiatione intenta ac affectuosa, quæ exigit caritatem. Loquitur etiam de confessione oris procedente ex fide formata. Fides autem sine operibus informis ac mortua est : ideo ejus confessio non sufficit ad salutem. Sed qui facit voluntatem, hoc est præceptum voluntatis, Patris mei qui in cœlis est, ipse intrabit post hujus exsilii incolatum, omniumque peccatorum plenam satisfactionem, in regnum cœlorum.
paras.en: That without good fruits no one can be saved the Saviour makes plain, adding: [[7:21|Not every one that saith to me|Non omnis qui dicit mihi]] from unformed faith [that is, faith without charity]: [[7:21|Lord, Lord|Domine, Domine]], as the foolish virgins did, [[7:21|shall enter into the kingdom of heaven|intrabit in regnum cœlorum]]: for the bare confession of the mouth is not enough. But against this seems the saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 12:3|no man can say The Lord Jesus, but by the Holy Ghost|Nemo potest dicere, Dominus Jesus, nisi in Spiritu Sancto]]; and again, [[Rom 10:10|For, with the heart, we believe unto justice: but, with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation|Corde creditur ad justitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem]]. It must be said that the Apostle takes “to say” properly, for an intent and affectionate utterance, which requires charity. He speaks too of the confession of the mouth that proceeds from formed faith. But faith without works is unformed and dead; therefore its confession is not sufficient for salvation. [[7:21|but he that doth the will|Sed qui facit voluntatem]], that is, the precept of the will, [[7:21|of my Father who is in heaven, he shall enter|Patris mei qui in cœlis est, ipse intrabit]], after the sojourn of this exile and full satisfaction for all his sins, [[7:21|into the kingdom of heaven|in regnum cœlorum]].

paras.t: Denique, ne fideles vanitate seducti, desiderent gratias gratis datas, ad excellentiam quamdam ac admirationem pertinentes, cujusmodi sunt prophetia, ejectio dæmonum, operatio miraculorum, quæ omnia bonis et malis sunt communia ; sed potius cupiant gratiam gratum facientem et veras virtutes, adjecit : Multi dicent mihi in die illa, hoc est, in die judicii, qui es dies famosissima. Ideo intelligitur, quamvis non exprimatur, distincte dicent, aut potius verbo mentali quam vocali, quic judicium illud celerrime fiet ac finietur quemadmodum infra asseritur : Sicut fulgur exit ab oriente, et apparet usque in occidentem ; sic erit adventus Filii hominis. Domine, Domine, nonne in nomine tuo, hoc est in te, et in virtute et gratia tua, prophetavimus? et in nomine tuo dæmonia ejecimus, videlicet invocando nomen tuum, et per illud demones adjurando? et in nomine tuo virtutes multas fecimus, hoc est multa miracula? Hæc non sufficiunt, quoniam Balaam divinitus prophetavit; et in Actibus quidam de circumeuntibus exorcistis Judæorum leguntur ejecisse dæmonia, dicendo : Adjuro vos per Jesum, quem Paulus annuntiat. Miracula quoque interdum fiunt, non merito operantis, sed recipientis, ad declarationem potentiæ Christi.
paras.en: Further, lest the faithful, led astray by vanity, should desire graces freely given [gratiae gratis datae, gifts such as prophecy and miracles, given for the good of others, as distinct from the grace that makes one holy] that belong to a certain eminence and to admiration, such as prophecy, the casting out of demons, and the working of miracles, all of which are common to good and bad, and should rather desire sanctifying grace and true virtues, He added: [[7:22|Many will say to me in that day|Multi dicent mihi in die illa]], that is, on the day of judgment, which is the most famous of days. It is understood, then, although it is not expressed, that they will say it distinctly, or rather by a mental than a vocal word, because that judgment will be made and finished most swiftly, as is said below: [[Matt 24:27|For as lightning cometh out of the east and appeareth even into the west|Sicut fulgur exit ab oriente, et apparet usque in occidentem]]: so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. [[7:22|Lord, Lord, have not we prophesied in thy name|Domine, Domine, nonne in nomine tuo prophetavimus]], that is, in Thee, and in Thy power and grace? [[7:22|and cast out devils in thy name|et in nomine tuo dæmonia ejecimus]], namely by calling upon Thy name, and adjuring the demons by it? [[7:22|and done many miracles in thy name?|et in nomine tuo virtutes multas fecimus]], that is, many miracles? These things are not enough, since Balaam prophesied by God’s gift; and in the Acts certain of the strolling exorcists of the Jews are read to have cast out demons, saying: [[Acts 19:13|I conjure you by Jesus, whom Paul preacheth|Adjuro vos per Jesum, quem Paulus]] [preaches]. Miracles too are sometimes worked not by the merit of the one who works them, but of the one who receives them, to declare the power of Christ.

paras.t: Et tunc confitebor, hoc est, per inspirationem internam, vel sententiæ contra eos prolationem, respondebo eis : Quia nunquam novi vos per absolutam approbationem, æternamque prædestinationem ; discedite a me in infernum, qui operamini etiamnunc, quantum ad affectum peccandi, iniquitatem. Quod enim in angelis casus, hoc in hominibus agit mors, secundum Damascenum. Quemadmodum ergo angeli æternaliter manent in illo affectu malitiæ in quo erant quando cadebant, sic anima æternaliter manet in illo affectu in quo recedit a corpore. Ideo reprobi jugiter erunt in affectu peccandi, et in die judicii, et in inferno : erit in eis desiderium peccandi, quamvis non poterunt illud exsequi. Unde Hieronymus et Chrysostomus dicunt : Non dicit, Qui operati estis, ne videatur tollere pœnitentiam, sed, Qui operamini, id est, qui usque in præsentem horam quum judicii tempus advenit, licet non habeatis facultatem peccandi, tamen adhuc habetis affectum. Sed opponi posset, quod in Sapientia de impiis legitur : Videntes turbabuntur timore horribili, intra se poenitentiam agentes. Dicendum, quod pœnitebunt de peccato, non in quantum est malum, sed in quantum est pœnæ meritorium.
paras.en: [[7:23|And then will I profess|Et tunc confitebor]], that is, by inward inspiration, or by pronouncing sentence against them, I will answer [[7:23|unto them, I never knew you|eis : Quia nunquam novi vos]] with absolute approval and eternal predestination; [[7:23|depart from me|discedite a me]] into hell, [[7:23|you that work iniquity|qui operamini iniquitatem]] even now, as regards the desire of sinning. For what the fall is in the angels, death works in men, according to Damascene. As, then, the angels remain eternally in the affection of malice in which they were when they fell, so the soul remains eternally in the affection in which it departs from the body. Therefore the reprobate will always be in the affection of sinning, both on the day of judgment and in hell: there will be in them the desire of sinning, although they will not be able to carry it out. Hence Jerome and Chrysostom say: “He does not say, ‘you who have worked’, lest He seem to take away penance, but, ‘you that work’; that is, you who up to this present hour, when the time of judgment has come, although you have not the means of sinning, yet still have the desire.” But it could be objected that we read in Wisdom of the wicked: [[Wis 5:2|These seeing it, shall be troubled with terrible fear|Videntes turbabuntur timore horribili]], [[Wis 5:3|Saying within themselves, repenting|intra se pœnitentiam agentes]]. It must be said that they will repent of sin not inasmuch as it is evil, but inasmuch as it is deserving of punishment.

paras.t: Omnis ergo, id est, quia confessio oris sine opere bono non sufficit, ideo omnis qui audit aure carnis et mentis, verba mea hæc, quæ in isto sermone disserui, in quo evangelicam legem proposui, et facit ea, bene vivendo, assimilabitur viro sapienti, qui ædificavit domum suam materialem supra petram, id est stabile fundamentum. Et descendit pluvia, et venerunt flumina, et flaverunt venti, et irruerunt in domum illam ; et non cecidit : fundata enim erat supra petram. Hoc enim totum litteraliter accipi potest de domo materiali, firmo fundamento subnixa : quam flumina, venti, et similia dejicere nequeunt, propter suæ constructionis stabilitatem. Tali igitur viro similis est omnis bonus Christianus, g2? ædificavit domum suam, id est conscientiam, vel operum suorum structuram, supra petram, videlicet Christum : de quo Apostolus, Petra (inquit) erat Christus ; et, Fundamentum aliud nemo ponere potest, præter id quod positum est, quod est Christus Jesus. Descendit pluvia, id est malarum suggestionum ac cogitationum tumultus seu copia, et venerunt flumina, id est persecutionum abundantia, et flaverunt venti, id est tumores elationis ac vanitatis, et irruerunt, id est, tentando impugnaverunt, domum illam, hoc est conscientiam piam, vel operationum bonarum congeriem, sibilante et invadente diabolo ; et non cecidit a via justitiæ : fundata enim erat supra petram, id est, Christo fortiter adhæsit, ejus gratiæ et adjutorio jugiter innitendo. Omnes enim qui sperant in eo, non infirmantur.
paras.en: [[7:24|Every one therefore|Omnis ergo]], that is, since the confession of the mouth without good work is not enough, therefore every one [[7:24|that heareth|qui audit]] with the ear of the flesh and of the mind [[7:24|these my words|verba mea hæc]] which I have set forth in this sermon, in which I have proposed the law of the Gospel, [[7:24|and doth them|et facit ea]] by living well, [[7:24|shall be likened to a wise man that built his house|assimilabitur viro sapienti, qui ædificavit domum suam]] of stone [[7:24|upon a rock|supra petram]], that is, a stable foundation. [[7:25|And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and they beat upon that house, and it fell not, for it was founded on a rock|Et descendit pluvia, et venerunt flumina, et flaverunt venti, et irruerunt in domum illam ; et non cecidit : fundata enim erat supra petram]]. All this can be taken literally of a material house resting on a firm foundation, which floods, winds and the like cannot throw down because of the stability of its construction. Like such a man, then, is every good Christian, [[7:24|that built his house|qui ædificavit domum suam]], that is, his conscience, or the structure of his works, [[7:24|upon a rock|supra petram]], namely Christ; of whom the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 10:4|and the rock was Christ|Petra (inquit) erat Christus]]; and, [[1 Cor 3:11|For other foundation no man can lay, but that which is laid: which is Christ Jesus|Fundamentum aliud nemo potest ponere præter id quod positum est, quod est Christus Jesus]]. [[7:25|And the rain fell|Descendit pluvia]], that is, the tumult or multitude of evil suggestions and thoughts, [[7:25|and the floods came|et venerunt flumina]], that is, the abundance of persecutions, [[7:25|and the winds blew|et flaverunt venti]], that is, the swellings of pride and vanity, [[7:25|and they beat upon|et irruerunt]], that is, assailed by tempting, [[7:25|that house|in domum illam]], that is, the devout conscience, or the mass of good works, while the devil hisses and attacks; [[7:25|and it fell not|et non cecidit]] from the way of justice: [[7:25|for it was founded on a rock|fundata enim erat supra petram]], that is, it clung strongly to Christ, leaning continually on His grace and help. For [[Ps 33:23|none of them that trust in him shall offend|Omnes enim qui sperant in eo]] [Denis: “all who hope in Him are not made weak”].

paras.t: Mystice per virum sapientem intelligitur Christus, qu? ædificavit per caritatem, fidem et gratiam, domum suam, id est Ecclesiam : quæ domus sumus nos; supra petram, id est in Deo Patre, de quo dicitur Dominus petra mea. Vel, Supra petram. id est fidei firmitatem, propter quam et de qua dictum est Petro : Tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram ædificabo Ecclesiam meam; itemque in Psalmo, Statuit supra petram pedes meos. In hanc domum. irruunt pluvia adversitatum, flumina, id est hominum persequentium agmina, venti, id est invisibiles hostes, spiritualia nequitiæ in cœlestibus, contra quos est nobis præcipua colluctatio; et non cadit, nec vincitur, quoad se totam, quoniam in Christo exstat fundata. Huic igitur sapienti viro, imo et sapientiæ Dei, pro viribus assimilemur, fundando et conservando corda ac opera nostra in Christo cum timore sancto et diligenti custodia, quia veraciter scriptum est : Si non instanter servaveris te in timore Domini, cito subvertetur domus tua.
paras.en: Mystically, by the wise man is understood Christ, [[7:24|that built|qui ædificavit]] by charity, faith and grace [[7:24|his house|domum suam]], that is, the Church, [[Heb 3:6|which house are we|quæ domus sumus nos]], [[7:24|upon a rock|supra petram]], that is, in God the Father, of whom it is said: [[2 Kings 22:2|The Lord is my rock|Dominus petra mea]]. Or, upon a rock, that is, upon the firmness of faith, on account of which and of which it was said to Peter: [[Matt 16:18|thou art Peter; and upon this rock I will build my church|Tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram ædificabo Ecclesiam meam]]; and likewise in the Psalm: [[Ps 39:3|he set my feet upon a rock|Statuit supra petram pedes meos]]. Upon this house rush the rain of adversities, the floods, that is, the hosts of men who persecute, and the winds, that is, the invisible enemies, [[Eph 6:12|the spirits of wickedness in the high places|spiritualia nequitiæ in cœlestibus]], against whom is our chief wrestling; and it does not fall nor is overcome as regards the whole of it, since it stands founded in Christ. To this wise man, then, indeed to the Wisdom of God, let us be likened according to our strength, founding and keeping our hearts and works in Christ with holy fear and diligent watchfulness, for truly it is written: [[Ecclus 27:4|Unless thou hold thyself diligently in the fear of the Lord, thy house shall quickly be overthrown|Si non instanter servaveris te in timore Domini, cito subvertetur domus tua]].

paras.t: Et omnis qui audit verba mea hæc auribus corporis solum, et non facit ea, obediendo præceptis meis jam introductis, similis erit viro stulto, qui ædificavit domum suam supra arenam, hoc est debile fundamentum. Et descendit pluvia, et venerunt flumina, et flaverunt venti, et irruerunt in domum illam; et cecidit, et fuit ruina ejus magna, id est, funditus eversa est, quia non habuit stabile fundamentum. Ad litteram planum est totum hoc. Talique stulto ædificatori parificatur homo sciens seu audiens verba Dei, nec tamen obediens. Ædificat enim domum suam, id est mentem, conscientiam, seu operationem, supra arenam, id est supra bonum creatum, variabile et caducum, videlicet supra humanam laudem, vanam gloriam, propriam adinventionem : idcirco a prædictis pluviis, ventis, ac fluminibus in ipsum ejusque domum irruentibus, cadit totaliter domus ipsius. Potest quoque per virum stultum dæmon intelligi, de quo in Evangelio dicitur : Inimicus homo hoc fecit. Qui domum suam, id est ecclesiam malignantium, supra prædictam arenam ædificat.
paras.en: [[7:26|And every one that heareth these my words|Et omnis qui audit verba mea hæc]] with the ears of the body only, [[7:26|and doth them not|et non facit ea]] by obeying My precepts now set forth, [[7:26|shall be like a foolish man that built his house upon the sand|similis erit viro stulto, qui ædificavit domum suam supra arenam]], that is, a weak foundation. [[7:27|And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and they beat upon that house, and it fell, and great was the fall thereof|Et descendit pluvia, et venerunt flumina, et flaverunt venti, et irruerunt in domum illam; et cecidit, et fuit ruina ejus magna]], that is, it was overthrown from its foundations, because it had no stable foundation. Literally all this is plain. And to such a foolish builder is compared the man who knows or hears the words of God and yet does not obey. For he builds his house, that is, his mind, conscience or activity, upon the sand, that is, upon a created good, changeable and perishable, namely upon human praise, vainglory, his own invention: therefore, when the rains, winds and floods mentioned rush upon him and his house, his house falls altogether. By the foolish man can also be understood the devil, of whom it is said in the Gospel: [[Matt 13:28|An enemy hath done this|Inimicus homo hoc fecit]]. He builds his house, that is, the church of the malignant, upon the sand described.

paras.t: Et factum est, quum consummasset, id est, prædicando finivisset, Jesus verba hæc, admirabantur turbæ super doctrina ejus, quoniam talia aut similia nunquam audierant a suis doctoribus. Erat enim docens eos sicut potestatem habens, hoc est gratiam efficacissimæ sermocinationis sortitus, qua corda audientium fortiter movit et excitavit, sicut de ipso Judæi dixerunt : Nunquam sic locutus est homo, sicut hic loquitur. Unde de ipso in Psalmo prædictum est : Diffusa est gratia in labiis tuis. Et Propheta : Posuit, ait, os meum quasi gladium acutum. Vel sic : Sicut potestatem habens, non solum ministerialiter, quasi servus, sed propria auctoritate, ut Dominus legis ac Prophetarum. Ideo non ea docuit solum quæ habentur in lege, sed legem exposuit, et supplevit, atque pro suo libito addidit et subtraxit. Et non sicut Scribæ eorum, et Pharisæi, qui tam efficaciter et auctoritative prædicare non poterant, sed tenebantur ad id quod Moyses in Deuteronomio jussit : Non adjicies ad verbum quod ego propono in conspectu tuo, nec subtrahes.
paras.en: [[7:28|And it came to pass when Jesus had fully ended these words|Et factum est, quum consummasset Jesus verba hæc]], that is, had finished preaching them, [[7:28|the people were in admiration at his doctrine|admirabantur turbæ super doctrina ejus]], since they had never heard such things or the like from their teachers. [[7:29|For he was teaching them as one having power|Erat enim docens eos sicut potestatem habens]], that is, endowed with the grace of most effective speech, by which He strongly moved and stirred the hearts of His hearers; as the Jews said of Him: [[John 7:46|Never did man speak like this man|Nunquam sic locutus est homo, sicut hic]]. Hence it was foretold of Him in the Psalm: [[Ps 44:3|grace is poured abroad in thy lips|Diffusa est gratia in labiis tuis]]. And the Prophet says: [[Is 49:2|he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword|Posuit os meum quasi gladium acutum]]. Or thus: as one having power, not only as a minister, like a servant, but by His own authority, as the Lord of the law and the Prophets. Therefore He did not teach only what is contained in the law, but expounded and supplied the law, and added and took away at His pleasure. [[7:29|and not as the scribes and Pharisees|Et non sicut Scribæ eorum, et Pharisæi]], who could not preach so effectively and with authority, but were bound to what Moses commanded in Deuteronomy: Thou shalt not add to the word which I set before thee, nor take away from it [cf. Deut 4:2].

8.title: Expositio capituli octavi: Quum autem descendisset de monte
8.title_en: Exposition of the eighth chapter: “And when he was come down from the mountain”

paras.t: Quoniam præinducta Christi doctrina supernaturalis est, humanæ rationis facultatem transcendens, neque argumentis humanis probabilis, ideo oportuit eam supernaturalibus argumentis, hoc est divinis miraculis, confirmari, ut sciretur esse a Deo, qui falsitatis assertor, aut confirmator esse non valet. Hinc ergo post evangelicæ doctrinæ descriptionem, describit beatissimus Evangelista Christi miracula : de quibus alibi Christus testatur, Opera quæ dedit mihi Pater, testimonium perhibent de me; et rursus, Si non venissem, et opera non fecissem quas nullus alius facere potest, peccatum non haberent, videlicet infideles Judæi. Hæc sunt divinæ veritatis verique Dei sigilla, Evangelio Christi appensa, quibus certissime scimus evangelicum librum esse velut epistolam, nobis a Deo per Christum transmissam, sicut et ipse fatetur : Mea doctrina non est mea, sed ejus qui misit me.
paras.en: Since the teaching of Christ set out above is supernatural, surpassing the power of human reason, and not to be proved by human arguments, it had to be confirmed by supernatural arguments, that is, by divine miracles, so that it might be known to be from God, who cannot assert or confirm what is false. Hence, after describing the teaching of the Gospel, the most blessed Evangelist describes the miracles of Christ, of which Christ testifies elsewhere: [[John 5:36|the works which the Father hath given me to perfect, the works themselves which I do, give testimony of me|Opera quæ dedit mihi Pater, testimonium perhibent de me]]; and again, [[John 15:24|If I had not done among them the works that no other man hath done, they would not have sin|Si non venissem, et opera non fecissem quæ nullus alius facere potest, peccatum non haberent]], namely the unbelieving Jews. These are the seals of the divine truth and of the true God, attached to the Gospel of Christ, by which we know most certainly that the book of the Gospel is like a letter sent to us by God through Christ, as He Himself declares: [[John 7:16|My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me|Mea doctrina non est mea, sed ejus qui misit me]].

paras.t: Ait itaque S. Matthæus : Quum autem descendisset Jesus de monte, in quo præscriptum fecit sermonem : qui non erat mons Oliveti, quamvis hoc dicat Chrysostomus, sed mons quidam in Galilæa, in qua fecit sermonem hunc, unde et statim fertur ingressus Capharnaum, quæ erat principalis urbs Galilææ : et hoc etiam dicit Hieronymus ; secuta sunt eum turbæ multæ, propter diversas rationes, ut tactum est supra.
paras.en: Saint Matthew says, then: [[8:1|And when he was come down from the mountain|Quum autem descendisset Jesus de monte]], on which He gave the sermon described above; which was not the Mount of Olives, though Chrysostom says so, but a mountain in Galilee, where He gave this sermon; hence He is said to have gone at once into Capharnaum, which was the chief city of Galilee; and Jerome too says this; [[8:1|great multitudes followed him|secutæ sunt eum turbæ multæ]], for various reasons, as was touched on above.

paras.t: Et ecce leprosus veniens, adoravit eum. Credidit eum esse verum Deum : quod utique Christus de se ipso in sermone præscripto insinuavit, dicendo : Multi dicent mihi in die illa : Domine, Domine, nonne in nomine tuo prophetavimus, et in nomine tuo dæmonia ejecimus, et in nomine tuo virtutes multas fecimus? quæ fieri non possunt, nisi in nomine Dei. Si ergo leprosus hoc intellexit, et Jesum Deum esse credidit, tunc dicendum, quod adoravit eum adoratione latriæ. Si autem credidit eum esse prophetam tantum et hominem purum, quamvis sanctum, adoravit eum veneratione duliæ, quæ creaturis impenditur : sicut et Josue adoravit angelum, et Salomon matrem suam, illa David regem. Adoravit ergo Jesum prostratus in terram, vel genibus flexis, dicens : Domine, si vis, potes me mundare. Quam fiducialis, vera, ac reverentialis petitio! Non enim de potentia subveniendi dubitavit, qui voluntatis pietatem imploravit. Certissimus fuit iste leprosus hominem illum amantissimum esse Deo, et omnia posse impetrare ab eo, cujus doctrinam tam potestativam efficacissimamque esse advertit. Et quoniam plena fide oravit, exaudiri mox meruit: omnia namque possibilia sunt credenti. Ideo subditur :
paras.en: [[8:2|And behold a leper came and adored him|Et ecce leprosus veniens, adoravit eum]]. He believed Him to be true God; which Christ indeed suggested of Himself in the sermon described, saying: [[7:22|Many will say to me in that day|Multi dicent mihi in die illa]]: Lord, Lord, have not we prophesied in thy name, and cast out devils in thy name, and done many miracles in thy name? which cannot be done except in the name of God. If, then, the leper understood this, and believed Jesus to be God, it must be said that he adored Him with the adoration of latria. But if he believed Him to be only a prophet and a mere man, though holy, he adored Him with the veneration of dulia [the honour given to creatures, as distinct from latria, the worship due to God alone], which is paid to creatures; as Josue too adored the angel, and Solomon his mother, and she King David. He adored Jesus, then, prostrate on the ground or on bended knees, [[8:2|saying: Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean|dicens : Domine, si vis, potes me mundare]]. How confident, true and reverent a petition! For he did not doubt His power to help, who implored the kindness of His will. This leper was most certain that that man was most beloved of God and could obtain all things from Him, whose teaching he perceived to be so full of power and so effective. And since he prayed with full faith, he deserved to be heard at once: for [[Mark 9:22|all things are possible to him that believeth|omnia namque possibilia sunt credenti]]. Therefore it is added:

paras.t: Et extendens Jesus manum suam, unitæ deitatis organum, tetigit eum, dicens : Volo, mundare, hoc est, volo ut munderis, ut legantur hæc verba divisim. In lege prohibitum erat tangere leprosum, sed hoc intelligendum erat de his qui maculari poterant a leproso, non de his qui suo tactu poterant purgare leprosum. Potuit vero Salvator sanare leprosum sine manus sua extentione et tactu; sed quia humanitatem assumpsit, per eam opemiratus est, et in agendo humano modo se habuit, ut sciamus totam salutem nostram per assumptam Christi humanitatem esse completam. Denique Christus dicendo, Volo, mundare, ostendit se esse de quo dictum est : Ipse dixit, et facta sunt. Et confestim mundata, id est repulsa seu ablata, est lepra ejus. In quo patet quam libere ac imperialiter operatus sit Christus, magisque mirandus est modus agendi, quam actio.
paras.en: [[8:3|And Jesus stretching forth his hand|Et extendens Jesus manum suam]], the instrument of the united Godhead, [[8:3|touched him, saying: I will, be thou made clean|tetigit eum, dicens : Volo, mundare]]; that is, I will that thou be made clean, so that these words are read separately [“I will” as one clause, “be thou made clean” as another]. In the law it was forbidden to touch a leper; but this was to be understood of those who could be defiled by the leper, not of those who by their touch could cleanse the leper. The Saviour could indeed have healed the leper without stretching out His hand and touching him; but since He had taken on humanity, He worked through it, and in acting behaved in a human way, so that we may know that our whole salvation was accomplished through the humanity Christ assumed. Moreover, by saying, I will, be thou made clean, Christ showed that He is the one of whom it is said: [[Ps 148:5|he spoke, and they were made|ipse dixit, et facta sunt]]. [[8:3|And forthwith his leprosy was cleansed|Et confestim mundata est lepra ejus]], that is, driven out or taken away. In this it is plain how freely and how royally Christ worked; and the manner of His acting is more to be wondered at than the action.

paras.t: Et ait illi Jesus : Vide, id est, perpende quod tibi injungo, videlicet, nemini dixeris quod curaverim te. Nonne in præsentia multorum Christus curavit hunc languidum, etiam ad suæ doctrinæ confirmationem ? Cur ergo jussit eum tacere ? Imo, si voluit miraculum esse occultum, cur non potius curavit eum silenter, solo nutu, seu voluntate, quam verbo et tactu? Et respondendum, quod jussit eum tacere : Primo, ut instrueret nos vanam gloriam devitare, et in mirificis actibus malle abscondi, quantum in nobis est, quam propalari, quamvis interdum propter aliorum profectum oporteat talia manifestari. Secundo, ut ait Hieronymus, quia necesse non erat ut voce jactaret, quod corpore præferebat. Tertio, secundum Chrysostomum, ne si fama sanationis ejus ad sacerdotes perveniret, recusarent eum, ex invidia Christi, tanquam mundatum admittere.
paras.en: [[8:4|And Jesus saith to him: See thou tell no man|Et ait illi Jesus: Vide, nemini dixeris]]; see, that is, weigh what I enjoin on thee, namely, tell no man that I have healed thee. Did not Christ heal this sick man in the presence of many, even to confirm His teaching? Why, then, did He bid him be silent? Indeed, if He wished the miracle to be hidden, why did He not rather heal him silently, by a nod alone, or by His will, than by word and touch? It must be answered that He bade him be silent: first, to teach us to avoid vainglory, and in wonderful deeds to prefer, as far as in us lies, to be hidden rather than made known, although sometimes for the profit of others such things must be made manifest. Secondly, as Jerome says, because there was no need for him to boast with his voice of what he showed in his body. Thirdly, according to Chrysostom, lest, if the report of his healing reached the priests, they should out of envy of Christ refuse to admit him as cleansed.

paras.t: Sed vade, ostende te sacerdotibus, ut illi judicent te mundatum, sicque inter homines converseris, et offer munus tuum, id est debitam oblationem Deo pro gratiarum actione beneficii tibi impensi, et pro emundatione tua, hoc est pro manifestatione tuæ purgationis, quod precepit Moyses a leprosis mundatis offerri, in testimonium illis, id est, ad hoc ut testimonium eis perhibeatur a sacerdote, quod sint vere a lepra purgati. Quemadmodum in Levitico legitur, jusserat Moyses ut leprosus mundatus offerret tortam panis, duosque turtures, atque sextarium olei, juxta ritum qui prædicto loco describitur. Christus, qui non venit legem solvere, nec cærimonialia reprobare ante suam passionem, misit leprosum mundatum, ut legalem hostiam immolaret, quoniam cærimonialia legis usque ad Christi passionem durabant, et vim obligandi habebant. — Porro, secundum Hieronymum, multis de causis mittit Christus leprosum ad sacerdotes : primo, ex humilitate, ut sacerdotibus videatur deferre; secundo, ne legem videatur infringere; tertio, ut sacerdotes vel credendo propter tantum miraculum salvarentur, vel non credendo inexcusabiles fierent. Est etiam alia ratio, scilicet figura futuri. Misit enim eum ad sacerdotem, ad figurandum quod Christianus, quamvis sit per contritionem et gratiæ infusionem a lepra animæ seu peccato mundatus, tenetur tamen congruo tempore, si adsit facultas, se sacerdoti novæ legis ostendere, aperiendo ei cor suum per veram confessionem, quia nec Deus dimittit peccatum, nisi sub hac conditione, videlicet, ut pœnitens proponat confiteri secundum Christi preceptum. — In Luca legitur iiste leprosus mundatus a Christo in una civitatum, puta Capharnaum.
paras.en: [[8:4|but go, shew thyself to the priest|Sed vade, ostende te sacerdotibus]], that they may judge thee clean, and so thou mayest live among men; [[8:4|and offer the gift|et offer munus tuum]], that is, the due oblation to God in thanksgiving for the benefit bestowed on thee, and for thy cleansing, that is, for the manifestation of thy cleansing, [[8:4|which Moses commanded|quod præcepit Moyses]] to be offered by cleansed lepers, [[8:4|for a testimony unto them|in testimonium illis]], that is, to the end that testimony be given them by the priest that they are truly cleansed from leprosy. As we read in Leviticus, Moses had commanded that the cleansed leper should offer a cake of bread and two turtle-doves and a sextary of oil, according to the rite described in that place. Christ, who did not come to destroy the law, nor to reject the ceremonies before His passion, sent the cleansed leper to offer the legal victim, since the ceremonies of the law lasted until the passion of Christ and had binding force. Further, according to Jerome, Christ sends the leper to the priests for many reasons: first, out of humility, that He may be seen to defer to the priests; secondly, lest He seem to break the law; thirdly, that the priests might either be saved by believing because of so great a miracle, or, by not believing, be made inexcusable. There is also another reason, namely a figure of what was to come. For He sent him to the priest to figure that a Christian, though he be cleansed from the leprosy of the soul, or sin, by contrition and the infusion of grace, is yet bound at a fitting time, if he has the opportunity, to show himself to the priest of the new law, opening his heart to him by true confession; for God does not forgive sin except on this condition, namely that the penitent purposes to confess according to Christ’s precept. In Luke we read that this leper was cleansed by Christ in one of the cities, namely Capharnaum.

paras.t: Quum autem introisset Capharnaum, accessit ad eum centurio, rogans eum, et dicens : Domine, puer meus jacet in domo paralyticus. Sciendum, quod iste centurio, id est princeps centum militum, seu hominum armatorum, non accessit ad Christum in propria persona, sed per alios a se missos, secundum quod Lucas dicit : Misit ad Jesum seniores Judæorum. At illi quum venissent ad Jesum, rogabant eum sollicite, dicentes ei : Quia dignus est ut illi hoc præstes; diligit enim gentem nostram, et synagogam ipse ædificavit nobis. Et post pauca : Me ipsum, inquit, non sum dignum arbitratus ut venirem ad te. Sed quia homo dicitur facere quod facit per alios, maxime per amicos, quemadmodum dicimus regem aliquem obsidere civitatem, eo quod populus ejus eo jubente eam obsideat; idcirco Matthæus asserit centurionem accessisse ad Jesum. Domine, puer meus jacet in domo paralyticus, id est, paralysim, utpote resolutionem ac immobilitatem membrorum et sensuum sustinens, et male torquetur, id est, gravissime infirmatur : quia (ut dicit Lucas) moriturus erat præ infirmitate. Et ait illi Jesus, hoc est, per alios respondit. Non enim immediate dixit ad centurionem verba sequentia. Ego veniam, et curabo eum. Quæritur, quomodo hoc verum sit, quod ait. Ego veniam : non enim venit usque ad centurionis domum, ut patet ex consequentibus. Ad hoc responderi potest dupliciter : Primo, quia (ut Lucas dicit) Jesus cœpit ire ad domum centurionis, et appropinquavit domui ejus, ideo ait, Veniam, scilicet usque ad locum domui tuæ propinquum. Secundo, ut intelligatur conditionaliter, scilicet, Ego veniam ad paralyticum domumque tuam, si desideraveris hoc : ut sit promissio benevolentiæ, non assertio operis.
paras.en: [[8:5|And when he had entered into Capharnaum, there came to him a centurion, beseeching him|Quum autem introisset Capharnaum, accessit ad eum centurio, rogans eum]], [[8:6|And saying, Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy|et dicens : Domine, puer meus jacet in domo paralyticus]]. It must be known that this centurion, that is, the commander of a hundred soldiers or armed men, did not come to Christ in his own person, but through others sent by him, as Luke says: [[Luke 7:3|he sent unto him the ancients of the Jews|Misit ad Jesum seniores Judæorum]]. [[Luke 7:4|And when they came to Jesus, they besought him earnestly, saying to him: He is worthy that thou shouldest do this for him|At illi quum venissent ad Jesum, rogabant eum sollicite, dicentes ei : Quia dignus est ut illi hoc præstes]]. [[Luke 7:5|For he loveth our nation: and he hath built us a synagogue|diligit enim gentem nostram, et synagogam ipse ædificavit nobis]]. And shortly after: [[Luke 7:7|neither did I think myself worthy to come to thee|Me ipsum, inquit, non sum dignum arbitratus ut venirem ad te]]. But since a man is said to do what he does through others, especially through friends, as we say that some king besieges a city because his people besiege it at his command, therefore Matthew asserts that the centurion came to Jesus. [[8:6|Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy|Domine, puer meus jacet in domo paralyticus]], that is, suffering paralysis, namely the loosening and immobility of the limbs and senses, [[8:6|and is grievously tormented|et male torquetur]], that is, is most gravely sick: for (as Luke says) [[Luke 7:2|was ready to die|moriturus erat]] from his sickness. [[8:7|And Jesus saith to him|Et ait illi Jesus]], that is, answered through others; for He did not say the following words directly to the centurion: [[8:7|I will come and heal him|Ego veniam, et curabo eum]]. It is asked how this is true which He says, I will come; for He did not come as far as the centurion’s house, as is plain from what follows. To this a twofold answer can be given. First, since (as Luke says) Jesus began to go to the centurion’s house and drew near to it, He therefore says, I will come, namely as far as a place near thy house. Secondly, that it be understood conditionally, namely, I will come to the paralytic and to thy house, if thou desire it; so that it is a promise of goodwill, not an assertion of the deed.

paras.t: Denique, propter magnam fidem, humilitatem, caritatem, ac sapientiam centurionis, Christus tam prompte promisit : Ego veniam, et curabo eum. Fides enim centurionis apparuit in hoc, quod credidit Christum posse curare letaliter infirmantem : quod non fuit multo minus miraculum quam suscitare defunctum. Humilitas, quod indignum se æstimavit in propria persona coram Christo apparere, vel eum in domo sua recipere : sicut et Petrus dixit, Exi a me, Domine, quia peccator sum. Caritas, quod pro servo suo tam instanter rogavit, quem etiam puerum nominat, propter dilectionem ad eum. Unde Lucas scribit, quod fuerat ei pretiosus, id est carus. Sicque centurio implevit illud Sapientis : Servus fidelis sit tibi quasi filius. Est quoque consuetudo Scripturæ, ministros pueros appellare. Unde in libris Regum habetur, quod Elias venit in Bersabee, et dimisit ibi puerum suum. Sapientia autem centurionis patet in hoc, quod Christi divinitatem cognovit, eumque solo verbo vel angelorum ministerio posse dare sospitatem pensavit.
paras.en: Moreover, because of the great faith, humility, charity and wisdom of the centurion, Christ promised so promptly: [[8:7|I will come and heal him|Ego veniam, et curabo eum]]. For the centurion’s faith appeared in this, that he believed Christ could heal one mortally sick; which was not much less a miracle than to raise the dead. His humility, in that he judged himself unworthy to appear before Christ in his own person, or to receive Him in his house; as Peter too said: [[Luke 5:8|Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord|Exi a me, Domine, quia peccator sum]]. His charity, in that he prayed so earnestly for his servant, whom he even calls his boy [puer, “boy”, also used for a servant], out of love for him. Hence Luke writes that he [[Luke 7:2|was dear to him|fuerat ei pretiosus]], that is, beloved. And so the centurion fulfilled the saying of the Wise Man: [[Ecclus 33:31|If thou have a faithful servant, let him be to thee as thy own soul|Servus fidelis sit tibi quasi filius]] [Denis: “as a son”]. It is also the custom of Scripture to call servants boys. Hence we have in the books of Kings that Elias [[3 Kings 19:3|came to Bersabee of Juda, and left his servant there|venit in Bersabee, et dimisit ibi puerum suum]]. And the centurion’s wisdom appears in this, that he knew the Godhead of Christ, and judged that He could give health by a word alone or by the ministry of angels.

paras.t: Denique ad dandum humilitatis exemplum, promisit se ad paralyticum servum iturum. Ut enim in Joanne habetur, rogatus visitare filium reguli, non acquievit ; sed rogatus visitare servum centurionis, statim assensit, ne dedignemur abjectas et pauperes visitare personas. In quo facto, secundum Gregorium, superbia nostra retunditur, qui in hominibus, non naturam qua ad imaginem Dei facti sunt, sed honores et divitias veneramur. Hinc ait Bernardus : Ad sanandum filium reguli ire noluit, ne divitias honorare videretur ; ad servum pergit, ne servilem conditionem contemnere putaretur.
paras.en: Moreover, to give an example of humility, He promised to go to the paralysed servant. For, as we have it in John, when asked to visit the son of the ruler He did not consent; but when asked to visit the centurion’s servant He agreed at once, that we may not disdain to visit lowly and poor persons. In this deed, according to Gregory, our pride is beaten down, who in men honour not the nature by which they are made to the image of God, but honours and riches. Hence Bernard says: “He would not go to heal the ruler’s son, lest He seem to honour riches; He goes to the servant, lest He be thought to despise the condition of a servant.”

paras.t: Et respondens centurio, ait : Domine, non sum dignus. Istam responsionem fecit centurio per nuntios intermedios. Quum enim aliqui retulissent ei verba Christi, Ego veniam, remisit nuntios ex parte sua, dicentes, Domine, non sum dignus, prout Lucas plenius recitat. Itaque, Non sum dignus ut intres sub tectum meum, hoc est in domum meam tecto opertam : quum tu sis genere Judæus, ego gentilis; tu Salvator, ego peccator ; tu Deus, ego homo. Quæ enim conventio luci ad tenebras ? Et quid tritico cum paleis? Agnovit centurio quam abominabile erat Judæis alienigenam accedere, vel cum gentilibus manducare, bibere, ingredi, vel misceri. Quidam dicunt, quod ideo dixit centurio, Domine, non sum dignus ut intres sub tectum meum, quia fortassis habuit idola in domo sua. Sed hoc non videtur probabile, quia (ut dictum est) ipse ædificavit synagogam Judæis : propter quod certum est quod fuerat fervens cultor unius veri Dei, sicut Cornelius centurio. Quis enim nunc sponte construeret Christianis ecclesiam, nisi coleret Christum? Sed tantum dic verbo imperiali, id est, dicendo præcipe ut puer meus sanetur, et sanabitur a paralysi puer meus : non enim est tibi difficile omne verbum. Unde habebat centurio iste tantam fidem de Christi potentia? Dicendum, quod partim ex fama qua audierat predictum leprosum tam potenter ac imperiose a Christo curatum, partim ex inspiratione divina. Præterea, quod non exigeretur corporalis præsentia Christi, probat per locum a majori. Nam et ego homo sum, videlicet homo purus, non Deus et homo ut tu, sub potestate constitutus, id est superiori principi subditus, utpote imperatori ac præsidi. Ex parte enim Romanorum positus fuit centurio in urbe Capharnaum, ut eam secundum legem Romanorum gubernaret et custodiret. Habens sub me milites centum mihi obedientes. Et dico imperando huic militi, Vade quo mitto te, et vadit ut jubeo; et alio (secundum antiquam grammaticam), id est, alteri militi dico, Veni ad me, et venit; et servo meo dico, Fac hoc quod tibi injungo, et facit. Per hæc verba dedit centurio intelligere, quod Christus solo precepto, atque angelorum obsequio, sine sua corporali præsentia, poterat facere omne quod voluit, nec indigeret ad curandum paralyticum corpore præsens esse.
paras.en: [[8:8|And the centurion, making answer, said: Lord, I am not worthy|Et respondens centurio, ait : Domine, non sum dignus]]. The centurion made this answer through intermediate messengers. For when some had reported to him Christ’s words, I will come, he sent messengers back on his own part, saying, Lord, I am not worthy, as Luke relates more fully. So: Lord, I am not worthy [[8:8|that thou shouldst enter under my roof|ut intres sub tectum meum]], that is, into my roofed house: since Thou art a Jew by race, I a Gentile; Thou the Saviour, I a sinner; Thou God, I man. For [[2 Cor 6:14|what fellowship hath light with darkness?|conventio luci ad tenebras]] And [[Jer 23:28|what hath the chaff to do with the wheat|quid tritico cum paleis]]? The centurion knew how abominable it was to the Jews for a foreigner to approach, or to eat, drink, enter or mix with Gentiles. Some say that the centurion said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof, because perhaps he had idols in his house. But this does not seem probable, since (as has been said) he himself built the synagogue for the Jews; for which reason it is certain that he was a fervent worshipper of the one true God, like Cornelius the centurion. For who now would of his own accord build a church for Christians unless he worshipped Christ? [[8:8|but only say the word|Sed tantum dic verbo]], the word of command, that is, command by speaking that my boy be healed, [[8:8|and my servant shall be healed|et sanabitur a paralysi puer meus]] of the palsy: for [[Jer 32:17|no word shall be hard to thee|non enim est tibi difficile omne verbum]]. Whence had this centurion such faith in Christ’s power? It must be said: partly from the report by which he had heard that the leper spoken of was healed so powerfully and so commandingly by Christ, partly from divine inspiration. Further, that the bodily presence of Christ was not required he proves by an argument from the greater. [[8:9|For I also am a man|Nam et ego homo sum]], namely a mere man, not God and man as Thou art, [[8:9|subject to authority|sub potestate constitutus]], that is, subject to a higher prince, namely the emperor and the governor. For the centurion had been placed by the Romans in the city of Capharnaum to govern and guard it according to the law of the Romans. [[8:9|having under me soldiers|Habens sub me milites]], a hundred, obedient to me. [[8:9|and I say to this, Go, and he goeth|et dico huic: Vade, et vadit]] [Denis glosses: “I say commanding to this soldier, Go where I send thee, and he goes as I bid”]; [[8:9|and to another Come, and he cometh|et alio (secundum antiquam grammaticam), id est, alteri militi dico, Veni ad me, et venit]] (alio is the older grammar for alteri, “to the other”), that is, I say to the other soldier, Come to me, and he comes; [[8:9|and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it|et servo meo: Fac hoc, et facit]], what I enjoin him. By these words the centurion gave to understand that Christ by a command alone, and by the service of angels, without His bodily presence, could do all that He willed, and did not need to be present in body to heal the paralytic.

paras.t: Audiens autem Jesus verba hæc ab ore nuntiorum, miratus est, vel vere, vel secundum apparatum, ut plenius inquiretur. Mimiratus est ergo de tam insolita fide, eximia humilitate, ingenti sapientia viri gentilis. Et sequentibus se turbis dixit: Amen, id est veraciter, dico vobis, non inveni tantam fidem in Isræl, id est in populo Judæorum, sicut in isto centurione. Non est hoc intelligendum de fide omnium Isrælitarum simul accepta, sed de fide cujusque seorsum. Secundum Hieronymum, Christus loquitur de præsentibus, non de præteritis Prophetis ac Patriarchis. Sed numquid fides centurionis major erat fide beatæ Virginis, Joseph, Zachariæ, Elisabeth, Simeonis et Annæ ? Non utique. Quomodo ergo intelligenda sunt hæc? Et respondendum, quod modicum pro nihilo reputatur, secundum Philosophum. Quoniam ergo Judæi in Christum perfecte credentes, paucissimi erant respectu aliorum non credentium (nondum enim fratres ejus in eum credebant, ut apud Joannem dicitur), ideo ait : Non inveni tantam fidem in. Isræl. Simili sensu ait in Psalmo, Et sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit; quum tamen scriptum sit, quod multæ mulieres sequentes plangebant eum, et discipuli ejus vehementissime contristabantur. Per Isræl ergo intelligit majorem partem Judæorum et principes eorum. Vel dicendum, quod ideo asserit se non invenisse tantam fidem, id est tam manifestam et excellentem fidei confessionem in Isræl, quoniam nemo Judæorum tempore conversationis Christi in mundo, tam publice ac præclare confessus est ejus majestatem sicut centurio, nisi forte paucissimis quibusdam exceptis, ut Joanne Baptista, etc.
paras.en: [[8:10|And Jesus hearing this, marvelled|Audiens autem Jesus miratus est]], from the mouth of the messengers, either truly or in outward appearance, as will be inquired into more fully. He marvelled, then, at the so unusual faith, the outstanding humility, and the great wisdom of a Gentile man. [[8:10|and said to them that followed him|Et sequentibus se turbis dixit]]: [[8:10|Amen I say to you, I have not found so great faith in Israel|Amen, id est veraciter, dico vobis, non inveni tantam fidem in Isræl]], that is, in the people of the Jews, as in this centurion. This is not to be understood of the faith of all the Israelites taken together, but of the faith of each one separately. According to Jerome, Christ speaks of those then present, not of the past Prophets and Patriarchs. But was the centurion’s faith greater than the faith of the Blessed Virgin, of Joseph, Zachary, Elizabeth, Simeon and Anna? Certainly not. How, then, are these words to be understood? It must be answered that a small amount is reckoned as nothing, according to the Philosopher. Since, then, the Jews who believed perfectly in Christ were very few in comparison with the others who did not believe (for [[John 7:5|neither did his brethren believe in him|nondum enim fratres ejus in eum credebant]], as is said in John), He therefore says: I have not found so great faith in Israel. In a like sense He says in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:21|And I looked for one that would grieve together with me, but there was none|Et sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit]]; though it is written that [[Luke 23:27|women, who bewailed and lamented him|mulieres sequentes plangebant eum]] [Denis: “many women following bewailed Him”], and His disciples grieved most vehemently. By Israel, then, He means the greater part of the Jews and their princes. Or it may be said that He asserts He has not found so great faith, that is, so manifest and excellent a confession of faith, in Israel, because no one of the Jews, in the time of Christ’s life in the world, confessed His majesty so publicly and so splendidly as the centurion, except perhaps a very few, such as John the Baptist, etc.

paras.t: Potest insuper dici, mystice intelligendum esse hoc dictum, videlicet de Ecclesia, respectu Synagogæ, non de persona centurionis et quocumque Judæo, ut sit sensus : Non inveni tantam fidem in Isræl, id est in Synagoga veteris Testamenti, sicut in centurione, id est in Ecclesia novæ legis, per centurionem designata, qui secundum doctores, figura fuit Ecclesiæ ex gentibus congregatæ. Sed tunc rursus dubium oritur, quomodo fides Ecclesiæ preferatur Synagogæ, quum Virgo benedicta, Apostoli, et tota pene Ecclesia primitiva, cujus fides perfectissima erat, fuerint ex populo Judæorum. Et respondendum, quod nomine Ecclesiæ, intelligi possunt omnes renati fonte Baptismatis : et sic fides Ecclesiæ major est fide Synagogæ, perfectione ac numero. Si autem per Ecclesiam intelligatur sola gentilitas conversa, seu Ecclesia ex gentibus adunata, sic fides Ecclesiæ major est fide Synagogæ, numero, id est credentium multitudine. Nam plures ex gentibus quam ex Judæis crediderunt in Christum. Aliqui etiam dicunt, quod fides centurionis præfertur fidei Isræl, et Apostolorum, discipulorumque Christi, non quantum ad devotionem, sed quantum ad facilitatem credendi.
paras.en: It can further be said that this saying is to be understood mystically, namely of the Church in respect of the Synagogue, not of the person of the centurion and any Jew whatever; so that the sense is: I have not found so great faith in Israel, that is, in the Synagogue of the Old Testament, as in the centurion, that is, in the Church of the new law, designated by the centurion, who according to the doctors was a figure of the Church gathered from the Gentiles. But then again a doubt arises how the faith of the Church is preferred to the Synagogue, since the Blessed Virgin, the Apostles, and almost the whole primitive Church, whose faith was most perfect, were of the people of the Jews. It must be answered that by the name of the Church can be understood all who are reborn of the font of Baptism; and so the faith of the Church is greater than the faith of the Synagogue in perfection and in number. But if by the Church is understood only converted Gentiledom, or the Church gathered from the Gentiles, then the faith of the Church is greater than the faith of the Synagogue in number, that is, in the multitude of believers. For more of the Gentiles than of the Jews believed in Christ. Some also say that the faith of the centurion is preferred to the faith of Israel and of the Apostles and disciples of Christ not as to devotion, but as to readiness in believing.

paras.t: Quod autem per centurionem figuretur fides Ecclesiæ ex gentilitate collectæ, hinc constat, quod Christus occasione fidei centurionis, de gentium conversione prædicit : Dico autem vobis, quod multi ab oriente et occidente, ac ceteris partibus terræ, quæ per duas principales partes mundi significantur, puta gentiles ex omnibus finibus mundi, venient ad fidem et gratiam per prædicationem Apostolorum : de quibus predictum est, In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum; quibus et dixit, Eritis mihi testes usque ad ultimum terræ. Hoc est quod Isaias inquit : Cantate Domino canticum novum, laus ejus ab extremis terræ. Ecce isti de longe venient, et ecce illi ab aquilone et mari, et isti de terra australi. Et recumbent, id est, feliciter requiescent, et spiritualiter edent ac bibent, cum Abraham et Isaac et Jacob, ceterisque electis Judæis, in regno cœlorum. Nominat autem Christus specialiter hos tres, quia inter Patriarchas præcipui, primi, ac famosissimi fuisse videntur, saltem in multis; et quoniam principaliter facta est eis promissio terræ repromissionis, per quam cœlestis figuratur hæreditas, seu regnum cœlorum.
paras.en: That by the centurion is figured the faith of the Church gathered from Gentiledom is clear from this, that Christ, on the occasion of the centurion’s faith, foretells the conversion of the Gentiles: [[8:11|And I say to you that many shall come from the east and the west|Dico autem vobis, quod multi ab oriente et occidente]], and the other parts of the earth, which are signified by two principal parts of the world, namely Gentiles from all the ends of the world, [[8:11|shall come|venient]] to faith and grace through the preaching of the Apostles; of whom it was foretold: [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum]]; and to whom He said: [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the uttermost part of the earth|Eritis mihi testes usque ad ultimum terræ]]. This is what Isaias says: [[Is 42:10|Sing ye to the Lord a new song, his praise is from the ends of the earth|Cantate Domino canticum novum, laus ejus ab extremis terræ]]. [[Is 49:12|Behold these shall come from afar, and behold these from the north and from the sea, and these from the south country|Ecce isti de longe venient, et ecce illi ab aquilone et mari, et isti de terra australi]]. [[8:11|and shall sit down|Et recumbent]], that is, shall rest happily, and spiritually eat and drink, [[8:11|with Abraham, and Isaac and Jacob|cum Abraham et Isaac et Jacob]], and the other chosen Jews, [[8:11|in the kingdom of heaven|in regno cœlorum]]. Christ names these three especially because they seem to have been the chief, the first and the most famous among the Patriarchs, at least in many respects; and because the promise of the land of promise, by which the heavenly inheritance or kingdom of heaven is figured, was made principally to them.

paras.t: Filii autem regni, id est Judæi increduli : qui dicuntur filii regni cœlestis, quia ad illud specialiter invitabantur, et quia in eis olim Deus regnavit, quum crederent in futurum, in quem non credebant prasentialiter apparentem, et inter eos conversantem. Isti ergo sunt filii vocatione et nomine, suaque præsumptuosa reputatione, non prædestinatione et vera consecutione. De quibus scriptum est : Provocaverunt eum filii sui et filiæ; et Isaias, Filios (inquit) enutrivi, ipsi autem spreverunt me. Hi ergo ejicientur a consortio electorum, in tenebras exteriores, id est corporales atque palpabiles tenebras carceris infernalis, statim quum moriuntur, quoad animam, in die autem novissimo, quoad corpus et animam. Tenebræ aliud non sunt nisi privatio luminis. Lumen vero est duplex, videlicet : spirituale, sicut est sapientia, gratia, veritas : et hujus privatio sunt tenebræ interiores, exsistentes in spiritu. Aliud est lumen sensibile, seu corporale : cujus privatio sunt tenebræ exteriores, quæ sequuntur per privationem, sicut silentium dicitur audiri. Quamvis autem in inferno sit ignis, ille tamen obscurus est atque fumosus, non lucidus, nisi forsitan in tantum ut damnati possint se mutuo videre ad cumulum suæ miseriæ, secundum Thomam. Potest quoque per tenebras istas infernus tenebrosus intelligi, qui propter suæ obscuritatis horribilem densitatem, nomine tenebrarum exprimitur. De quo ait beatus Job : Dimitte me antequam vadam ad terram tenebrosam, et opertam mortis caligine.
paras.en: [[8:12|But the children of the kingdom|Filii autem regni]], that is, the unbelieving Jews, who are called children of the heavenly kingdom because they were specially invited to it, and because God once reigned in them when they believed in Him who was to come, in whom they did not believe when He appeared present and lived among them. These, then, are children by calling and name and by their own presumptuous reckoning, not by predestination and true attainment. Of them it is written: [[Deut 32:19|his own sons and daughters provoked him|provocaverunt eum filii sui et filiæ]]; and Isaias says: [[Is 1:2|I have brought up children, and exalted them: but they have despised me|Filios (inquit) enutrivi, ipsi autem spreverunt me]]. These, then, [[8:12|shall be cast out|ejicientur]] from the fellowship of the elect [[8:12|into the exterior darkness|in tenebras exteriores]], that is, the bodily and palpable darkness of the prison of hell, at once when they die as to the soul, and on the last day as to body and soul. Darkness is nothing else than the privation of light. Now light is twofold: spiritual, such as wisdom, grace and truth, and its privation is the interior darkness that exists in the spirit; the other is sensible or bodily light, whose privation is the exterior darkness, which is perceived through privation, as silence is said to be heard. And although there is fire in hell, it is dark and smoky, not bright, except perhaps so far that the damned can see one another to the heaping up of their misery, according to Thomas. By this darkness can also be understood dark hell, which because of the horrible thickness of its obscurity is expressed by the name of darkness. Of it blessed Job says: [[Job 10:21|Before I go and return no more, to a land that is dark and covered with the mist of death|antequam vadam ad terram tenebrosam, et opertam mortis caligine]] [Denis: “Let me alone before I go …”].

paras.t: Ibi, videlicet in inferno seu tenebris ejus, erit fletus, et stridor dentium. Certum est quod fletus et stridor dentium non sint corporaliter in substantiis spiritualibus, scilicet animabus separatis atque dæmonibus ; sed ante diem judicii est in eis fletus interior, id est summa tristitia, ex qua corporalis fletus solet causari, et dentium stridor, id est interiorum viscerum horrenda concussio. Post diem vero judicii, erit in hominibus condemnatis stridor dentium corporalis ex frigore infernali, quoniam ibunt a calore nimio ad aquas nivium. In fletu autem corporali duo pensantur, videlicet oculorum ac cerebri conturbatio, et resolutio lacrimarum. Quantum ad primum erit in eis fletus, non quantum ad secundum, quia cessante motu primi mobilis, omnis generatio atque corruptio finem habebit. Talis etiam fluxus seu resolutio lacrimarum tandem finiretur, nisi Deus miraculose multiplicaret in illis materiam lacrimarum, puta humorem in corpore.
paras.en: [[8:12|there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth|ibi erit fletus et stridor dentium]], namely in hell or its darkness. It is certain that weeping and gnashing of teeth are not bodily in spiritual substances, namely separated souls and demons; but before the day of judgment there is in them interior weeping, that is, the deepest sorrow, from which bodily weeping is usually caused, and gnashing of teeth, that is, a horrible shaking of the inward parts. But after the day of judgment there will be in condemned men a bodily gnashing of teeth from the cold of hell, since [[Job 24:19|Let him pass from the snow waters to excessive heat|ad nimium calorem transeat ab aquis nivium]] [Denis reverses the order: “they shall go from excessive heat to the snow waters”]. Now in bodily weeping two things are weighed, namely the disturbance of the eyes and the brain, and the shedding of tears. As to the first there will be weeping in them, not as to the second, because, when the motion of the first heaven ceases, all generation and corruption will come to an end. Such a flow or shedding of tears would also come to an end at last, unless God miraculously multiplied in them the matter of tears, namely the moisture in the body.

paras.t: Et dixit Jesus centurioni, per internuntios : Vade, id est, ab hac tua sollicitudine et timore recede, securusque esto; et sicut credidisti puerum tuum posse sanari solo verbo meo me absente, fiat tibi ut ille curetur. Et sanatus est puer in illa hora, imo eodem, ut puto, momento quo Christus verba hæc protulit, vel quo centurio ea audivit.
paras.en: [[8:13|And Jesus said to the centurion|Et dixit Jesus centurioni]], through the messengers: [[8:13|Go|Vade]], that is, withdraw from this anxiety and fear of thine, and be secure; [[8:13|and as thou hast believed|et sicut credidisti]] that thy boy could be healed by My word alone in My absence, [[8:13|so be it done to thee|fiat tibi]], that he be healed. [[8:13|And the servant was healed at the same hour|Et sanatus est puer in illa hora]]; indeed, as I think, at the very moment in which Christ uttered these words, or in which the centurion heard them.

paras.t: Quæritur circa prædicta, quomodo in Christo fuit admiratio? Ad quod aliqui dicunt, quod in Christo non fuit vera admiratio, quia ut asserit Damascenus, admiratio ex subita imaginatione alicujus novi procedit, videlicet ex nova et repentina apprehensione alicujus insoliti prius incogniti, vel non considerati. Christus autem ut homo, a primo suæ conceptionis instanti vidit, actualiterque cognovit in Verbo visione beatifica, omnia quæ cognoscit Verbum notitia visionis, hoc est omnia quæ unquam fuerunt, vel erunt : ideo nil de novo apprehendit, unde ad admirationem inductus sit. Sed fuit in eo admiratio secundum exteriorem apparentiam : quæ non fuit deceptoria, sed ordinata ad nostram instructionem, videlicet, ut fidem centurionis, aliorumque mirificam conversionem, et Judæorum perfidiam admiremur. Sic nempe et Deus per modum mirantis se habuit, quum de Sodomitis loqueretur in Genesi : Descendam, et videbo si juxta clamorem qui venit ad me faciant. Alii dicunt, quod in Christo fuit vera admiratio, non quantum ad scientiam beatificæ visionis, nec quantum ad scientiam habitualem infusam, qua cognovit res in proprio genere, sed quantum ad scientiam acquisitam et experimentalem, quam isti ponunt in anima Christi. Sic ergo secundum istos, fuit in Christo aliquid de novo cognitum, prius ignotum, quoad istum sciendi modum seu habitum, ex cujus inspectione admirabatur.
paras.en: Concerning what has been said it is asked how there was wonder in Christ. To this some say that there was no true wonder in Christ, because, as Damascene asserts, wonder proceeds from the sudden imagining of something new, namely from a new and sudden apprehension of something unusual, previously unknown or not considered. But Christ as man, from the first instant of His conception, saw and actually knew in the Word, by the beatific vision, all that the Word knows by the knowledge of vision, that is, all things that ever were or will be; therefore He apprehended nothing new by which He could be led to wonder. But there was wonder in Him according to outward appearance; which was not deceitful, but ordered to our instruction, namely that we should wonder at the faith of the centurion and the marvellous conversion of the others, and at the faithlessness of the Jews. For so God too behaved after the manner of one wondering when He spoke of the Sodomites in Genesis: [[Gen 18:21|I will go down and see whether they have done according to the cry that is come to me|Descendam, et videbo si juxta clamorem qui venit ad me faciant]]. Others say that there was true wonder in Christ, not as to the knowledge of the beatific vision, nor as to the infused habitual knowledge by which He knew things in their own kind, but as to the acquired and experimental knowledge which these writers place in the soul of Christ. So, according to them, there was in Christ something newly known and previously unknown as regards this mode or habit of knowing, from the consideration of which He wondered.

paras.t: Postremo, moralitatem breviter tangendo, sicut per centurionem figuratur Ecclesia, ita per servum ejus paralyticum figuratur quilibet spiritualiter languidus, et maxime acediosus, more paralytici ad divina piger, et quasi immobilis. Pro tali orat Ecclesia Christum, ut puerum hujusmodi curet, et ad divina fervidum agilemque efficiat : cujus precibus Christus frequenter annuit. Et sicut centurio ex humilitate misit seniores Judæorum intercessores, sic Ecclesia per sacerdotes tanquam per mediatores implorat Christi clementiam : quorum fide, prece ac merito, peccatores frequenter sanantur, quemadmodum fide centurionis sanatus est puer ejus. Per centurionem quoque, qui dixit humillime, Domine, non sum dignus ut intres sub tectum meum, figurati sunt timorati ac humiles Christiani, qui Christi opem desiderant, sed eum intra se communicando vel celebrando recipere vehementer verentur: unde eum spirituali receptione Sacramenti multoties contentantur. Et quamvis hoc interdum sit bonum, melius tamen est ex fervore et spe pietatis divinæ Sacramentum recipere. Semper autem expedit cum centurione, Christi dignitatem, propriamque vilitatem perpendere, et intimo corde fateri : Domine, non sum dignus, etc. Per puerum quoque seu servum paralytieum, convenienter intelligitur appetitus sensitivus totus infectus, et ad mala proclivus, qui jacet in domo nostra, videlicet corpore fragili, in quo, secundum Apostolum, non habitat bonum. Hunc ergo petamus sanari a Christo, ut sine rebellione serviat rationi ac Deo.
paras.en: Lastly, to touch briefly on the moral sense: as the Church is figured by the centurion, so by his paralysed servant is figured anyone spiritually sick, and above all the slothful [acediosus, one afflicted with acedia, spiritual sloth], who like a paralytic is sluggish and as it were motionless towards divine things. For such a one the Church prays Christ to heal this boy and make him fervent and active towards divine things; and Christ often grants her prayers. And as the centurion out of humility sent the elders of the Jews as intercessors, so the Church implores the clemency of Christ through priests as mediators; by whose faith, prayer and merit sinners are often healed, as the centurion’s boy was healed by his faith. By the centurion too, who said most humbly, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof, are figured God-fearing and humble Christians, who desire Christ’s help but greatly fear to receive Him within themselves by communicating or celebrating; hence they are often content with the spiritual reception of the Sacrament. And although this is sometimes good, yet it is better to receive the Sacrament out of fervour and hope in the divine kindness. But it is always expedient with the centurion to weigh the dignity of Christ and one’s own vileness, and to confess from the inmost heart: Lord, I am not worthy, etc. By the boy or paralysed servant can also fittingly be understood the sensitive appetite, wholly infected and prone to evil, which lies in our house, namely the frail body, in which, according to the Apostle, [[Rom 7:18|there dwelleth not in me, that is to say, in my flesh, that which is good|non habitat in me, hoc est in carne mea, bonum]] [Denis: “good does not dwell”]. Let us ask, then, that it be healed by Christ, so that it may serve reason and God without rebellion.

8.title: Prosecutio expositionis præsentis capituli: Et quum venisset Jesus in domum Petri
8.title_en: Continuation of the exposition of the present chapter: “And when Jesus was come into Peter’s house”

paras.t: Recitatis duobus miraculis in sexu virili peractis, describitur tertium factum in sexu femineo. Utrumque etenim sexum venit Christus corporaliter spiritualiterque sanare congruo ordine. Et quum venisset Jesus in domum Petri apostoli, qui erat in civitate Capharnaum, quamvis Petrus esset de civitate Bethsaida, ut legitur in Joanne. Solebat enim Christus divertere ad domus familiarium suorum et amicorum, ad quiescendum atque vescendum, non ex necessitate, sed ex dignatione. Vidit socrum ejus, hoc est matrem uxoris Petri, jacentem et febricitantem, ut habetur in Luca, quod tenebatur magnis febribus. Erat enim vetula, quæ multum debilitabatur ex febribus, propter defectum naturalis caloris. Et tetigit Jesus manum ejus, ut habetur in Marco, quod accedens elevavit eam tenens manum ejus; et dimisit eam, id est, recessit ab ea, febris repente, quia (ut Lucas ait) imperavit febri et continuo surrexit. In quo signo magis mirandus est modus agendi, quam actio. Quamvis enim naturaliter possit quis sanari a febribus, non tamen in instanti, sed hoc supernaturale est. Et surrexit socrus sanata, et ministrabat eis ad mensam, vel aliis, utpote Christo et ejus discipulis. In quo aliud signum consideratur, quia (ut dicit Hieronymus) natura febricitantium est, ut post febrem corpora magis lassescant, et incipiente sanitate, mala pristinæ ægritudinis sentiant. Quod ergo hæc mulier subito vires perfecte recepit, certum est supernaturale fuisse.
paras.en: Having related two miracles worked on the male sex, the Evangelist describes a third done on the female sex. For Christ came to heal both sexes, bodily and spiritually, in fitting order. [[8:14|And when Jesus was come into Peter’s house|Et quum venisset Jesus in domum Petri]] the apostle, which was in the city of Capharnaum, although Peter was of the city of Bethsaida, as we read in John. For Christ was wont to turn aside to the houses of His intimates and friends to rest and to eat, not out of necessity but out of condescension. [[8:14|he saw his wife’s mother|vidit socrum ejus]], that is, the mother of Peter’s wife, [[8:14|lying, and sick of a fever|jacentem et febricitantem]]; as we have it in Luke, that she [[Luke 4:38|was taken with a great fever|tenebatur magnis febribus]]. For she was an old woman, much weakened by the fevers through the failing of natural heat. [[8:15|And he touched her hand|Et tetigit Jesus manum ejus]], as we have it in Mark, that [[Mark 1:31|coming to her, he lifted her up, taking her by the hand|accedens elevavit eam tenens manum ejus]]; [[8:15|and the fever left her|et dimisit eam febris]], that is, went away from her suddenly, because (as Luke says) [[Luke 4:39|he commanded the fever|imperavit febri]], and at once she rose. In this sign the manner of acting is more to be wondered at than the action. For although someone can be healed of fevers naturally, yet not in an instant; that is supernatural. [[8:15|and she arose and ministered to them|Et surrexit socrus sanata, et ministrabat eis]], the mother-in-law, being healed, at table, or to the others, namely Christ and His disciples. In this another sign is considered, because (as Jerome says) it is the nature of those who have had a fever that after the fever their bodies grow more weary, and as health begins they feel the ills of the former sickness. That this woman suddenly recovered her strength perfectly, then, was certainly supernatural.

paras.t: Vespere autem facto, videlicet die isto ad occasum tendente, obtulerunt ei, videlicet Christo, multos dæmonia habentes, id est dæmoniacos ; et ejiciebat spiritus malignos ab obsessis corporibus, verbo, id est solo vocis suæ imperio, non longa adjuratione, ut exorcista Judæorum. Ab instanti enim quo Christi humanitas unita fuit Verbo personali unione, subjecta est ei omnis creatura : ideo ejus imperio omnia creata obediunt. Propter quod ait Salvator : Pater diligit Filium, et omnia dedit in manu ejus. Et omnes male habentes, id est infirmos, curavit. Vicini namque, perceptis præscriptis miraculis, adduxerunt ad Jesum omnes languidos suos, curavitque universos. Ut impleretur quod dictum est per Prophetam, dicentem : Ipse infirmitates nostras accepit, et ægrotationes portavit. Nostra translatio continet sic, Vere languores nostros ipse tulit, et dolores nostros ipse portavit : et redit in idem. Ut sit sensus : Ipse Christus infirmitates, id est pœnalitates nostras, ex originali peccato consecutas, videlicet mortalitatem, famem, sitim, lassitudinem, ceterosque indetrahibiles defectus, accepit in se ipso, et habuit eas, sicut ait in Psalmo : Infirmata est in paupertate virtus mea; et rursus, Ego sum pauper et dolens; itemque, Repleta est malis anima mea. Et ægrotationes portavit, id est, nostros languores pie in aliis supportavit, et condolendo curavit, sicut Apostolus dicit : Alter alterius onera portate. Non tamen fuit in Christo infirmitas corporalis ex indispositione complexionis proveniens, secundum Damascenum. Non ergo assumpsit omnes defectus nostros, sed eos dumtaxat qui integritati et perfectioni naturæ non repugnant.
paras.en: [[8:16|And when evening was come|Vespere autem facto]], namely as that day drew towards sunset, [[8:16|they brought to him many that were possessed with devils|obtulerunt ei multos dæmonia habentes]], namely to Christ; that is, demoniacs; [[8:16|and he cast out the spirits|et ejiciebat spiritus]], the evil ones, from the possessed bodies, [[8:16|with his word|verbo]], that is, by the command of His voice alone, not by long adjuration like the exorcists of the Jews. For from the instant in which Christ’s humanity was united to the Word by personal union, every creature was made subject to it; therefore all created things obey its command. For this reason the Saviour says: [[John 3:35|The Father loveth the Son: and he hath given all things into his hand|Pater diligit Filium, et omnia dedit in manu ejus]]. [[8:16|and all that were sick he healed|et omnes male habentes curavit]]. For the neighbours, having seen the miracles described, brought all their sick to Jesus, and He healed them all. [[8:17|That it might be fulfilled, which was spoken by the prophet|Ut impleretur quod dictum est per Prophetam]], [[8:17|saying: He took our infirmities, and bore our diseases|dicentem : Ipse infirmitates nostras accepit, et ægrotationes portavit]]. Our translation has it thus: [[Is 53:4|Surely he hath borne our infirmities and carried our sorrows|Vere languores nostros ipse tulit, et dolores nostros ipse portavit]]; and it comes to the same. So that the sense is: He, Christ, [[8:17|took our infirmities|infirmitates nostras accepit]], that is, the penalties that followed from original sin, namely mortality, hunger, thirst, weariness and the other defects that cannot be taken away, took them upon Himself and had them; as He says in the Psalm: [[Ps 30:11|My strength is weakened through poverty|Infirmata est in paupertate virtus mea]]; and again, [[Ps 68:30|But I am poor and sorrowful|Ego sum pauper et dolens]]; and likewise, [[Ps 87:4|For my soul is filled with evils|Repleta est malis anima mea]]. [[8:17|and bore our diseases|Et ægrotationes portavit]], that is, He bore our sicknesses lovingly in others, and healed them by suffering with them; as the Apostle says: [[Gal 6:2|Bear ye one another’s burdens|Alter alterius onera portate]]. Yet there was not in Christ bodily infirmity arising from an ill-disposed constitution, according to Damascene. He did not, then, take on all our defects, but only those which are not contrary to the integrity and perfection of nature.

paras.t: Videns autem Jesus turbas multas circa se : quia ut dicit Marcus, tota civitas erat congregata ad januam; jussit ire secum discipulos suos trans fretum, id est ultra mare Galilææ, quod juxta Capharnaum decurrebat. Abiit ergo navigio a Capharnaum in locum desertum, ut Lucas et Marcus commemorant, ut doceret nos humanam laudem et gloriam fugere, tunc præsertim quando magnum aliquid egimus, et magis ab universis cum admiratione inspicimur. Quum enim prædicta miracula faceret, omnes in ejus præconium proruperunt. Dæmones quoque copiose clamabant, dicentes, Tu es Christus et Filius Dei, sicut alii referunt Evangelistæ.
